//: Story Phase 7, chapter 35: Not a Stenchmaster Duty. The captain orders the Grand Stenchmaster to help. The crew invoke the emergency labour rule from Phase 5 (it is nailed to the mainmast, and it even says SHARKS). Garrick's loophole: these are not shipboard sharks but meteorological ones, and the rule only covers emergencies within the reasonable operational scope of the Grand Stenchmaster: Meteorological Shark Management is a different department. Then the job description, again, with the obvious answers forbidden (wear the suit, fart, watch television, be lazy); the three primary functions (eating, sleeping, farting); television as a support function (boredom interferes with digestion); 'Ye have invented a government office for being lazy.' 'At last, someone understands.' 'THAT WAS NOT PRAISE.' And the Grand Sharkmaster: the office that ought to handle the consequences of his office. It does not exist. That, says Garrick, is a staffing problem.
p7c3.begin: captain[angry]: Garrick. The ship is being attacked. By a storm. That YOU made. I am ordering ye to help.
garrick[businesslike]: Of course, Captain. I'd love to. Unfortunately, it isn't a Stenchmaster duty.
pete[annoyed]: The emergency rule! It's nailed to the MAST!
rook[annoyed]: 'In any genuine ship emergency!' It's a genuine ship emergency! There's SHARKS in it!
garrick: I'm familiar with the rule, Mister Rook. I was there when it was nailed. I think you'll find it has a scope.
garrick[smug]: Read it to me, Captain. Out loud. Carefully. I think you'll find it supports my position.

p7c3.begin.tutorial: Fetch the emergency labour rule (nailed to the mainmast) and read it to him.
p7c3.begin.title: Not a Stenchmaster Duty

p7c3.rule: You wrench the nails out of the mainmast with the back of your cutlass and pull the rule down. Extra nails. You remember putting them in.
Under your signature, in green crayon, very small: 'ONE (1).' Underneath that: 'WE ARE COUNTING.' Underneath THAT, in a third hand: 'STILL COUNTING.'

p7c3.rule.tutorial: Read it to the Grand Stenchmaster (his chair).
p7c3.rule.title: Not a Stenchmaster Duty

p7c3.read: You hold the rule up in front of his face, so close the paper touches his monocle.
captain[angry]: 'In any genuine ship emergency. SHARKS. The Center. Fire. Sinking. All of the above. The Grand Stenchmaster will do AT LEAST one useful thing.'
captain[angry]: SHARKS, Garrick. It says SHARKS.
garrick[businesslike]: Ship sharks, Captain.
captain: ...What?
garrick[businesslike]: Sharks in the water, under the ship, eating the hull. Shipboard sharks. I'd be the first to help with those. These, on the other hand...
garrick[businesslike]: ...are in the SKY. They're weather. This is Meteorological Shark Management. A completely different department.
crew: IT IS NOT!

garrick: And there's an implied clause, of course. 'Within the reasonable operational scope of the Grand Stenchmaster.' It doesn't need writing down. Otherwise it would be unreasonable, and you, Captain, are a reasonable man.
captain[angry]: I am NOT a reasonable man. I am a PIRATE.
garrick: Besides, I did my one useful thing. In the spring.
crew: AT LEAST ONE!
gristle[annoyed]: It says AT LEAST! 'At least' means MORE!
garrick[offended]: 'At least' is a floor, Mister Gristle. Not a ceiling. I'm standing on the floor.
hale[annoyed]: Right. RIGHT.
Hale has fetched the slate from the galley, and a lump of chalk, and is writing on it with his teeth gritted.
hale[annoyed]: We're doing this properly this time. Once and for all. What does the Grand Stenchmaster ACTUALLY DO?
hale: And before you start: you are not allowed to say any of these.
garrick[alarmed]: ...That rules out several important departments.
hale[annoyed]: GOOD.
garrick[nervous]: Very well. Very well. Let me simplify the office for you. The Grand Stenchmaster has three primary functions.
garrick[businesslike]: One. EATING. That provides the raw material.
garrick[businesslike]: Two. SLEEPING. That conserves Grand Stenchmaster energy.
garrick[proud]: Three. Farting. That produces the official stench.
pete[annoyed]: That's just being ALIVE, badly!
garrick[offended]: It is NOT. Anyone can be alive. Very few people can be alive at THIS level.
rook[annoyed]: And the television? Where's that? That's not on your three!
garrick[businesslike]: The television is a support function.
rook: A WHAT?

garrick[businesslike]: Boredom, Mister Rook, interferes with relaxation. Relaxation is necessary for sleeping. Sleeping is necessary for digestion. And digestion is necessary for eventual Grand Stenchmaster output.
garrick[proud]: So the television, if you follow it all the way down, is part of the production line.
There is a long silence while the crew follow it all the way down.
bob: ...He's built a whole... system. To prove that watching television helps him fart.
gristle[disgusted]: He's built a GOVERNMENT.
captain[angry]: Ye have invented a government office for being lazy.
garrick[delighted]: At last, someone understands!
captain[angry]: THAT WAS NOT PRAISE!
p7c3.sharkmaster: captain[angry]: Listen to me. Every shark on this ship is here because of the smell. The smell is YOURS. The consequences of your stench are YOUR responsibility.
garrick[businesslike]: I disagree, Captain. Respectfully. And with the support of the organisational chart.
captain: There isn't an organisational chart.

garrick: There will be. The Grand Stenchmaster creates and manages the stench. That's my office. The consequences of the stench, the sharks and so forth, are properly the responsibility of a Grand Sharkmaster.
Everyone stops. Even the storm seems to pause for a moment, as if it would like to hear this too.
captain[surprised]: ...What?
garrick[businesslike]: The Grand Stenchmaster manages the stench. The Grand Sharkmaster manages the sharks. It's very simple.
bob[surprised]: There IS no Grand Sharkmaster!
garrick[proud]: Exactly. That's a staffing problem.
gristle[annoyed]: YE JUST INVENTED ANOTHER OFFICE!
garrick[businesslike]: Organisational development.
pete[annoyed]: So we need another man whose whole job is fixing the disasters caused by YOUR job?
garrick[smug]: Now ye understand management.
captain[tired]: I understand nothing.
bob[concerned]: ...Where do we even hire a Grand Sharkmaster?
Garrick gestures, vaguely, out over the rail, at the open sea.
garrick: The pirate employment market?
A shark goes past at head height, mouth open, very close.
pete[annoyed]: THE MARKET IS FULL OF SHARKS!
garrick: Hm.
The Grand Stenchmaster watches the shark go, and strokes his whiskers thoughtfully.
garrick[businesslike]: We could hire one of them, I suppose. They know the field.
garrick[worried]: ...No. No. Conflict of interest.
Rook sits down on the deck in the rain and puts his head between his knees. Bob pats him on the back without looking at him.
hale[resigned]: I'm writing it on the slate. GRAND SHARKMASTER. So it's on record that this happened.
garrick[proud]: Thank you, Mister Hale. Put 'vacant'. I'll draw up a notice.
